Howdy y'all!!

Huge thanks to everyone who came back to try our FROSTBURN update! We're happy that y'all have enjoyed it, and it's been awesome to see the new melee weapons and frost spells finding their way into your builds.

Everything on the tech side has been going really well and we're blown away by how many of y'all showed up for more cowbyerous adventures

STATS FOR STAT NERDS

we put uh yeah some stats together for the stat lovers in our community. here u go

🧊 60,000+ brand new players?? 🧊

🌋 11,000+ concurrent players?! 🌋

😡 500+ bugs reported? 😡

We're hard at work fixing all the MANY many MANY many bugs y'all have reported, and we are working as fast as we can to release a patch that will fix most of them, while also balancing the things you have given feedback on. ALSO we're focusing on stabilizing the game on low-end specs and on Linux 😁👍

A new devlog should also drop very soon to show you what we're working on for the next patch! And don't forget to take a look at our new roadmap if you haven't already: https://farfarwest.notion.site/

Have a nice day

items.content:
Howdy y’all! 

Frostburn is officially out now!

Before we get into everything that’s packed into this update, we wanted to quickly follow up on something we mentioned in our last post.

We know it’s been a little quiet from us for a while, and we said we’d start opening the curtains a bit more on what’s happening behind the scenes. The truth is, the last few months absolutely knocked us sideways. The release was a huge moment for our small team, and after everything that came with it, we needed some time to rest and recover. From here on out, we’ll be sharing more regular progress updates and dev blogs, so you can follow along with how Far Far West is coming together.

We’ve also put together a roadmap for Far Far West, giving you a rough idea of what we’re planning to add to the game and when you can expect to see it. Obviously, things can change at any time as development continues, but we wanted to give you a better idea of where we’re heading.

-> ROADMAP <-

FFW ON DISCOUNT!

ALSO! For the next TWO WEEKS Far Far West will be discounted by 20%! So if you or your pals have been waiting for some new content or a sweet discount to ride into the west, FROSTBURN is for y’all!

(Discount asset?)

Alright, enough talk. Let’s get into the…

FROSTBURN UPDATE!

DISCLAIMER!!

Last final small disclaimer:

There have been some issues with AMD Frame Generation across multiple titles. If you encounter any kind of performance issues or crashes, please make sure to try turning AMD FSR ON or OFF. AMD is looking to release a patch to resolve this issue soon, so please bear with us! <3

FEATURES/CONTENT

⚔️ITEM FRAGMENTS 

The way item fragments worked was complicated, and not many people understood it until they had a few games under their belt. It was also a big hassle to remember to start tracking another item every time you were done with one. This new system simplifies everything by making them a universal currency.

  • Item Fragments are now called Blueprints

    [/*]

  • Tracking items to earn their blueprints is gone. You now collect blueprints during missions like you do any currency, and can then use them at the lobby

    [/*]

  • You no longer need to pay gold to buy a weapon after unlocking it. Spending blueprints to unlock them will directly purchase them

    [/*]

  • 🚨 All your accumulated blueprints on each weapon have been aggregated and converted to the unique blueprint currency 🚨

    [/*]

🚨 LIGHTHOUSES 

We figured that most of the time, people almost never stumbled upon the Copy Press, the Refiner, or any other unique location, even though they did spawn in the mission. The main way to find them was to recognize their shape on the mini-map. Well, we’re adding a proper way of discovering what spawned on your map through lighthouses!

  • Lighthouses spawn in every mission and are indicated on your mini-map

    [/*]

  • Reaching the top of a lighthouse (we know you’ll use spells to cheat your way up) and completing its minigame reveals the map and its unique locations

    [/*]

☢️ URANIUM

You previously had to spend Gold to buy, copy or refine jokers during your games, which was annoying since Gold is also the money used to unlock long-term things in the lobby. We’re adding a new currency that only exists in-mission, so that using the tools available in-game never feels like a waste anymore. You also earn Uranium by completing quests & secrets, making sure replaying either of those is never useless. Finally, as the joker list keeps expanding, so does the chance of stumbling upon jokers you don’t like. You’ll now be able to break those jokers and get Uranium instead, then spend it on whatever you want.

  • Anything that costs currency during a mission now uses Uranium instead of Gold

    [/*]

  • Leftover Uranium at the end of a mission is converted into XP for your hero and your weapons

    [/*]

  • Uranium can be collected in different ways:

    • Break a Joker \[NEW: hit a Joker with your fists to break it]

      • The amount of Uranium depends on the rarity of the broken joker

        [/*]

      • Dropped jokers do not give Uranium

        [/*]
      [/*]

    • Kill an Elite enemy

      [/*]

    • Complete a secondary objective

      [/*]

    • Complete a quest

      [/*]

    • Complete a secret

      [/*]

    • Complete a lighthouse

      [/*]

    • Unique Uranium objectives

      [/*]

    • Flying balloons

      [/*]
    [/*]

🥊 MELEE WEAPONS

MELEE WEAPOOOOOOOOOOONS! You’ve asked for them A LOT, and here they are! Melee weapons bring a new way of playing Far Far West, each with its own playstyle, just like the ranged weapons. They don’t use a dedicated slot and will replace either your primary or your secondary weapon, so make sure you can still kill every enemy with your setup before going into missions! This is only the first batch of melee weapons, more will come along the way :)

PRIMARY SLOT MELEE WEAPONS:

  • Knuckles: Short range, big impact. Requires no ammo, no aim, and no thoughts.

    [/*]

  • Right-click: send out a damaging burst in a wide cone

    [/*]

  • \ \[⚪⚪⚪] FIST RO DAH: The charged attack propels you backwards and has a 20% chance to apply Frost to enemies

    [/*]

  • \ \[⚪⚪⚪] FIST RAGE: Taking damage generates charge and grants +30% attack speed for 2 sec.

    [/*]

Lasso: Whips enemies fast at a decent reach. Some of them come back for more, and not out of spite.

  • Right-click: deal damage to all enemies in front of you for a few seconds

    [/*]

  • \ \[⚪⚪⚪⚪] SKY LASH: The charged attack grants +50% move speed and lets you fly

    [/*]

  • \ \[⚪⚪⚪] SPELL LASH: Casting a spell instantly fills your charge bar

    [/*]

SECONDARY SLOT MELEE WEAPON: 

  • Banjo: Slow and weak attacks, some healing power. Perfect for healing your allies while destroying their eardrums.

    [/*]

  • Right-click: heal yourself and your allies in a zone around you

    [/*]

  • \ \[⚪⚪⚪⚪⚪] LULLABARD: Gain an extra chord per hit and a wider healing zone, but lose the slam attack

    [/*]

  • \ \[⚪⚪⚪⚪⚪] BARDBARIAN: Hold the slam attack longer to release a more powerful blow

    [/*]

🛡️ SHIELD POINTS

Losing HP happens a lot in Far Far West. We’re also adding melee weapons, which means being in melee range, and even more occasions to lose HP. To keep your screen from constantly going red while unlocking a new playstyle, we’re introducing a shield system!

  • Shield Points can be gained in different ways, such as using specific jokers, weapons or Frost spells

    [/*]

  • Shield Points are shown above your HP bar and take damage first, protecting your HP

    [/*]

  • Shield Points automatically decay over time when you stop gaining them for a few seconds or aren’t taking damage

    [/*]

  • Shield Points have a maximum capacity of 100

    [/*]

📈 UPGRADES

WEAPONS:

  • RANGE: Increases the range of your melee weapons

    [/*]

  • CHARGING SPEED: Increases the rate at which your melee weapons charge

    [/*]

🃏 JOKERS - WEAPONS

A LOTTA BUNCH OF JOKERS! Some of them are pretty standard and only slightly buff statistics, but that also means they work for your build most of the time. With the amount of jokers constantly growing, the amount of jokers you don’t want grows just as fast, so having basic jokers around makes sure you have more chances of stumbling upon something useful. Another bunch of jokers was added to support melee weapons, as none of the base jokers were designed with melee in mind. This should make sure that melee is a fully playable playstyle! Obviously, the joker list will keep on growing in the future, always focused on providing new playstyles and balancing them.

🧊 FROST ELEMENT

With melee weapons and the new shield system coming in, we needed a new element to support these new playstyles. The Frost element is here to provide spells that fit well with melee weapons, but it can also stand on its own and provide utility to your allies!

Defensive - Freeze enemies and reinforce your shield

items.content:
Howdy, y’all!

We know it’s been a while.

We’ve seen the comments, the questions, the “when update?” messages. We know you’ve been waiting, and we really appreciate y’all sticking with us

The honest answer is that a lot has been happening behind the scenes

We’re a small indie team, and when we launched Far Far West into the world, we definitely didn’t expect the level of love and success that came our way. It’s been AMAZING!! But it’s also meant taking a step back and making sure we were ready for what comes next.

Over the last few months, we’ve been doing a lot of work that isn’t particularly exciting to show in a trailer, reworking internal structures, expanding the team, improving how we work, and figuring out what the future of Far Far West should actually look like.

We’ve been taking our time with this because we want to hold ourselves to the same standards we’ve always had for the game. We don’t just want to throw updates out the door for the sake of having something to show.

And now, we’re ready to start showing you what we’ve been working on.

Introducing the FROSTBURN UPDATE!

On August 27th, our next major update for FFW arrives

Full details on the update will be available on launch day! For now put your guesses for the update in the comments 

Play Frostburn First at Gamescom

If you’re heading to Gamescom, you’ll actually be able to get your hands on Frostburn a full 24 HOURS before anyone else.

🗓️26th August, 1PM (CET) | Booth 131, Hall 10.2

Come say hi, play the new update, let us know what you think and grab your very own FFW cowboy hat (while stocks last). We can’t wait to meet y’all!

Thanks again for hanging around while we’ve been busy behind the scenes. We know the wait hasn’t been the most fun, but we think you’ll understand why we took the time once you start seeing what we’ve been working towards.

The dust is starting to settle. Frostburn is coming.

See y’all in the Far (Far) West

- The Far Far West Team 🤠🌵

items.content:
🔥 THIS SUMMER, WE’RE COOKING 🔥

(It’s really hot outside..)

Howdy y'all!

Welcome to a big catch-up devlog covering most of what the team has cooked up between the last update and early July 👽

So, what’s been happening behind the curtain? Let’s take a look!

Keep in mind that everything below is WORK IN PROGRESS and might not ship as shown. We’re still cookin’ for now!

The Zurkers keep crawling out of the spaceship

Our new sci-fi invader faction, the Zurkers, keeps on growing! Their faces are a bit glitchy for now, since we still haven’t managed to get them to sign a release form for their image rights.

(Actually, we’re still in the early stages of the army and have a LOT of work to do before showing anything too detailed to you all.)

Concepts & 3D models by @Capp and @MashArt / Textures and rigs by @Adrian

New exploration POIs: Lighthouses

A new family of Lighthouse points of interest is now scattered across the maps. If you’re careful enough with your jumps, you’ll learn a lot more about your surroundings!

Instead of getting the Anvil, Refiner, and Copy Press revealed for free on the minimap, you’ll now have to climb lighthouses and water towers, then play a minigame to reveal the whole map! The idea is to reward decision-making, not pure luck. You can still stumble onto any hidden structure by exploring on foot, but a lighthouse will light your way with ease.

This feature is still WIP and needs some balancing and polish (sounds, VFX)

Level Design by @Promium / Level Art by @Erton

The Jungle map needs some explorers!

Mysterious places have been spotted deep in the Jungle… A questline has been added! Explore 3 underground dungeons and collect all the ancient scrolls to unlock the brand-new Hellfire map!

There’s also a secret, but since it’s a secret, I can’t tell you there’s one.

Level Design by @Promium / Level Art by @Erton

The Hellfire map

The Hellfire map is almost done, and it’s already crawling with Cryptics waiting to ambush you.

Level Design & Level Art by @Erton

The Redwood Forest map

Work has started on a brand-new map: a giant redwood forest. Think towering trees wrapped in climbable wooden platforms, with vertical paths to fight your way through. Very early days for now!

Level Design & Level Art by @Erton

Melee weapons… are COMING!

It’s time to get up close and personal, don’t you think?

A whole rack of melee weapons is cooking! We’re still working out exactly how they’ll play and how to balance them with the rest of the game, which is why there’s not much footage to show just yet!

Concepts & 3D models by @Capp and @MashArt / Textures and rigs by @Adrian

Skins? SKIIIIIIIIIINS!

The art team has also whipped up some fresh skins!

Original fanart by community member @Swolf, reworked and modeled by @Capp - The Aviator

Concept & 3D model by @MashArt - Bullet Bob! The new weapon smith!

Concept & 3D model by @Capp - Arizona Jones, the Jungle quest NPC!

Rig by @Adrian

A new element? Definitely. A most-requested one? For sure.

I’ll just leave you with a screenshot that should be more than enough of a visual clue to guess what it is.

And since I love to cultivate mystery, I’m sending this one along too. (It’s a shield.) (This is no longer a mystery.) (The shield mechanic is coming.)

Jokers. More Jokers. And after that, even more Jokers.

We’re adding some quality-of-life improvements to Jokers! We’re also cooking up a LOT (30+) of new Jokers, some designed specifically to make melee builds viable. It’s a first step toward our bigger goal of diversifying builds!

Two new members on the team!

We’ve had two fresh faces join the crew recently!

PROmium is here to handle a whole bunch of level design and programming stuff, from quests to enemies and more. The man fears nothing.

Teeto will handle everything tech-related, meaning more programming stuff, but not the same kind of programming stuff. There are a lot of different kinds of programming stuff, you know. He’s currently working on our network, a Discord integration, a Twitch integration, and a lot more internal tools to make our lives at Evil Raptor easier!

Thanks for readin'

There’s still plenty we’re working on that didn’t make it into this devlog, but for now, that’s it for this peek behind the curtain! Again, all of this is WIP, no gameplay, and some of it might change a lot or never ship

THANK YOU for playing Far Far West and sticking with us <3

See you in the next one.

And without further ado, onto the patch notes!

FEATURES

Enemies

Most feedback that we received regarding the higher difficulties were that is was too simple and not challenging enough, with some people managing to win games without picking up any joker during their mission. These changes aim to make the Nightmare difficulty more challenging, hence giving an incentive to complete side objectives and collect jokers throughout the game. This is obviously just a small portion of what we want to do to increase the challenge of higher difficulties!

New Elite enemies!

They are bigger, stronger, bolder!

Elite Prowlers

Run faster, spam attacks, lot of HP. Real stalkers.

Elite Liches

spawn 3 shockwaves instead of 1 and summon semi-homing projectiles. Also lot of HP!

Elite Slingers

items.title: Far Far West Essential Beginner Guide
Far Far West is the indie co-op shooter we’ve been waiting for
items.summary: I had this review for Far Far West written long before it flew to 1 Million sales, and I'm glad to see I predicted correctly
items.content:
Games like Warhammer 40,000 Darktide , Warhammer 40,000 Space Marine and Warhammer 40,000 Helldivers manage to have permanent progression and level-based blasting without going so hard on the roguelike elements, but indies tend to avoid that space. Gunfire Reborn , Abyssus and that new Painkiller game (Sorry for reminding you) all commit to roguelike, procedural maps and random drops each run. That’s not inherently a bad time, but it can leave a fellow hankering for something more bespoke.

What Far Far West lacks in character upgrades it more than makes up for in a perfect difficulty ramp, diverse spell list, persistent bespoke worlds and weirdly wonderful objectives.

Right off the bat Far Far West oozes with that semi-low-poly look that made Gunfire Reborn so fun to blast through. This time, though, we’re all saddled up in the wild west complete with saloons, stables and steampunk trains. Robotic farm animals roam about, and the train pulls up to the station in the game’s hub to take you off to a mission.

When you arrive, you’ll want to saddle up. The robotic steeds of Far Far West are your get-out-of-jail card for tight situations, as well as a way to make traversing the large open-maps more fun. Not only are you faster out on the open plains, but your horse can also jump you higher and make use of carriages dotted around that catapult you even further.

The gunplay is smooth (Once you turn acceleration off for controller players), hit feedback is exceptional and the ragdoll effect of enemies (Or bits of enemies) makes weapons feel powerful. It also clearly communicates when something is dead, which is vital in more hectic shoot-outs where target prioritisation and quick thinking is the key to victory.

Like most shooters of this kind you need to keep moving to keep alive, but without a sprint function the game is more reminiscent of a Halo co-op campaign than a nu-DOOM style movement shooter. Movement on foot is deliberate and picking of enemies at the right moment really matters. This cycle between grounded, weighty movement on foot contrasted to the fast, fluid movement on horseback is fantastic for engagement — keeping the maps from feeling too sluggish.

Once your boots do hit the ground you won’t just be slinging lead (Or arrows, or Sheriff Stars that act like Suriken) as you have access to 3 spell slots. These slots can be assigned 1 spell each from the list of 25+ available, ranging from fire magic to cactus summoning and even using the power of voodoo.

If that diversity wasn’t enough, just wait until you and your friends all spam spells at once…

I was levelling cactus magic (as one does) and so had been routinely deploying a cactus mine, which waits for enemy movement then detonates 3 times in quick succession. The “ plonk, plonk, plonk ” of the detonations was well-established in my brain as a cue that my mine was going off.

My co-op partner (Hi Alex) was levelling voodoo with the goal of unlocking a new revive spell for us in harder difficulty modes. Once, during a particularly hectic defence objective, I’d thrown down my cactus mine and my partner snapped her fingers for her voodoo magic to seek out enemies at the same time. Suddenly, our ears were assaulted with 3 consecutive tolls of doom-guiding bells…

Her voodoo magic had hit my cactus mine, infusing the 3 explosions it normally has with the power of voodoo, and adding the thematic bell toll effect to each explosion. It took us accidentally triggering the interaction two more times to realise what was happening, and even longer to realise that enemies hit by this combo were brainwashed onto our side! Bear in mind nothing about the cactus mine brainwashes, and the voodoo ability in question was for lifesteal only. This means spell combinations can actually create new effects for combat, not just combine two effects into one.

From then on, I’d always call out when I had a mine about to blow so that it could be infused — be it with voodoo, fire, acid or lightning. In a party of four players the number of combinations would be exponentially higher still, and I can imagine some niche applications for dedicated players. The other combination we found was that calling an orbital laser onto a patch of electrified cloud creates a fire tornado. If that doesn’t sound over-the-top and fun to pull off, I just think maybe the game isn’t for you.

All this juicy combat takes place in open-world style maps. Each map is hand-crafted without procedural generation. Objectives can spawn in different places and different POIs can be active, but the maps are explorable and learnable across multiple missions. This might sound like a bad thing, since the maps could become stale, but fortunately Far Far West combats that in a few ways:

While increasingly harder areas and missions will inherently burn through more ammo and resources, Far Far West does some of the best work I’ve seen in the genre to avoid just padding enemies with stats. Difficulty increases add new enemy types, increase enemy density and add “Danger Zones” to maps that provide combat and navigational challenges. If a danger zone overlaps an objective, you’re in for a rough fight with hordes of enemies.

items.title: Far Far West publisher says "We don't work with partners that are relying on generative AI"
items.summary: Fireshine Games CEO Brian Foote warns that generative AI assets are a "red line"
items.content:
Fireshine Games CEO Brian Foote warns that generative AI assets are a "red line"

Image credit: Evil Raptor/Fireshine Games News by Lewis Packwood Features Editor Published on May 19, 2026, 12:26 p.m. Fireshine Games, the publisher behind Steam hit Far Far West, has said it won't work with developers that use generative AI art.

"We don't work with partners that are relying on generative AI or generative art, and I think that's the red line we are very clear on," said Fireshine CEO Brian Foote in an exclusive interview with GamesIndustry.biz .

But Foote added that the publisher will allow the use of some generative AI development tools.

"If AI means code completion or means using Copilot in Word, that's an entirely different set of scenarios," he said. "It will be very hard for anybody to say they're not touching AI in some way, shape or form, but in terms of the core game creation, that is not something that we think players are interested in at this point in time, and not something that we think is healthy for the development community."

"As it stands, it's something that we are firm on," he concluded.

Tim Bender, CEO of the Manor Lords publisher Hooded Horse, made a similar proclamation in January , extending to the use of generative AI for placeholder assets. "We recommend they don’t use any gen AI anywhere in the process," he said, explaining that there's a chance AI-generated art might slip through to the finished game.

Far Far West, developed by the French studio Evil Raptor, has proven to be a breakout hit on Steam since its launch into Early Access on April 28. Fireshine recently announced that the western-themed co-op shooter has sold more than one million copies within its first two weeks on sale.
